findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: The review criterion describes commit markers as plain lines (`**Commit**:`), but this file writes them as checkbox tasks (e.g. `- [ ] **Task 2C: Commit** — ...`). This is consistent with the project's own convention (AGENTS.md: "Each item and subitem should have a `[ ]` checkbox") and with the completed sibling slice `260-tasks.onboarding-consolidation.md`, which uses the identical `**Task nC: Commit** —` checkbox form. The substantive requirement — markers at working, tested points, not after every task and not only at the end — is satisfied (2C, 3C, 5C, 6C, 8C, 9C, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15C). No action needed; noted only because it deviates from the literal marker format.

findings.title: Renderer tests exercise reachable outcomes only, not literally "every outcome"
findings.description: The Technical Requirements say `renderAdoptionFacts` should be tested for "every outcome." `AdoptionOutcome` has five kinds; Task 8T exercises `brownfield`, `adoption-in-progress`, and `NOT_EVALUATED`, omitting `greenfield`, `already-planned`, and `adoption-closed`. This is defensible: the resolver only renders facts when selected (D4 step 3 = brownfield / adoption-in-progress / explicit), so the other three kinds are unreachable in production and the exhaustive `never` switch already forces them to compile. Impact is therefore near-zero. If literal coverage of the requirement is wanted, adding a `greenfield` case is the cheapest close, since it is the source-bearing sibling of `brownfield` and would catch a regression in the "source volume when the outcome carries it" branch.

findings.title: Task 5's parenthetical about gitExec's timeout message is imprecise
findings.description: Task 5 states "gitExec's timeout message already reads `timed out after 5s`." The real rejected message wraps that detail: `git {args} failed in {cwd}: timed out after 5s`, and `withNetworkErrorHint` then appends offline-remediation text because `/timed out after \d+s/i` matches. This does not break anything — Task 5T wisely mocks gitExec to reject with exactly `timed out after 5s` and asserts only that `reason` *contains* `timed out`, which is robust to the wrapping. The practical consequence is that the `history: unknown` reason rendered in the Adoption Facts section will be the full wrapped string (command + cwd + network hint), not the bare phrase. Worth the implementer knowing so the verbose reason in the facts bullet isn't a surprise; no change to the task logic is required.
